protocol.identityKFitOn: all NFL team identities in preceding validation season, never held-out caller outcomes
protocol.productionComparison: current tendency.py, both prior three seasons and all prior available seasons
protocol.target: recorded pass vs run under current production classification; QB scrambles are runs
protocol.outcomeAccess: all fitting seasons precede each outer test season

limits: Only one transferring play caller is covered. Unmapped teams and seasons remain unknown; they are never assigned the head coach by default.
Official reports establish the primary role, not a snap-by-snap audit. Shared decisions and unreported temporary delegation may remain.
Published retrospective role confirmation does not reveal play outcomes to the model; nevertheless this is reconstructed historical metadata, not a database archived before each kickoff.
The 2026 caller change is source-backed context and a boundary test only. No 2026 outcomes enter training or evaluation.
One coach and one transfer: game bootstrap intervals describe these Denver games, not coach-to-coach generalization.
Quarterbacks, injuries, opponent, roster quality, personnel and formation are not controlled. Associations are not causal coaching effects.
This uses finalized play-by-play and reconstructs pre-snap fields, not the live payloads that were actually available before kickoff.
A context-model result is an offline finding, not authorization to ship revised live probabilities or claim a learning effect.
The fixed 50/50 transfer blend is exploratory; several comparisons are reported and no multiple-testing correction is applied.
